questions: Are you short of breath or worse when you take a deep breath?
Do you have any new leg swelling or pain (especially in one leg), or recent long travel/immobility/surgery in the past 4 weeks?
Do you have a fever or any recent cough/upper respiratory symptoms (and if yes, what color is the sputum)?
What is your current temperature and oxygen saturation (if you know it), and have you noticed any coughing up blood (hemoptysis)?
Have you had any recent chest injury or new heavy lifting/strain that could explain chest wall tenderness?
Have you had your chest pain worse when leaning forward or better when sitting up and leaning forward?
Have you had any recent ECG changes or lab tests showing elevated troponin (heart muscle injury) or any clinician told you you have pericarditis?
answers: Yes—my chest pain gets worse with deep breaths, and it feels pleuritic. I also get trouble breathing when I lie down (orthopnea).
No, I don’t have new leg swelling or pain in one leg, and I haven’t had recent long travel or immobility or surgery in the past 4 weeks.
I recently had a viral infection, but I’m not having a new fever that I know of. I don’t have a recent cough or sputum to describe.
I don’t know my temperature or oxygen saturation. And no—I haven’t noticed coughing up blood.
No, I don’t remember any chest injury or new heavy lifting/strain. The pain feels sharp and “knife-like,” but it doesn’t seem tied to an injury.
Yes, it feels worse with leaning forward, and it’s a bit better when I sit up.
I haven’t had any recent ECG changes or troponin tests that I know of. But yes—I've been told before that I had pericarditis.
